Subject: Post-call recap — deployment gating items (SSO / KMS / logs)

Hi Erin / Tom —

Thanks again for the productive call today. Quick recap of what we heard and the gating items that will drive whether MedFoundry needs a Private (VPC/on‑prem) deployment vs Redwood Dedicated:—

Summary of constraints we captured in the call:
- Identity: You require enterprise SSO (SAML/Okta) + SCIM for group sync for RBAC.
- Keys: HSM-backed customer keys for model data (FIPS-certified HSM preferred). BYOK with strict key separation is a hard requirement for regulated workloads.
- Logs/Retention: Audit logs and request/response metadata must be retained for 7 years and exported to your SIEM. You also need fine-grained per-tenant access logs.
- Data residency: US only, with potential on-prem evaluation for air-gapped PII workflows.

What this implies from our side: Dedicated can meet SSO (SAML + SCIM) and supports customer-managed KMS (BYOK) with cloud KMS integrations, but does not provide tenant-dedicated HSMs in the multi-tenant Dedicated offering. For guaranteed HSM-backed isolation and full physical separation, Private (VPC or on‑prem) is the path we recommend.

Immediate asks from MedFoundry (items we need to progress):
1) Procurement timeline & decision owner (ProcureOps contact) — will you target a 60–90 day PO window?
2) Confirmation on whether an initial Dedicated pilot (90 days) is acceptable with the explicit understanding HSM requirement is a road‑map item for Private later.
3) Technical: sample IP ranges for allowlists, SOC2 report recipient address, and the specific retention policy language you require for logs (e.g., immutable retention / WORM).

I've attached a short deployment matrix to show tradeoffs (mf_deployment_matrix.xlsx).

Next steps / proposed owners:
- Sean: coordinate commercial proposal & pilot terms (by 10/23)
- Laura: propose technical configuration for a Dedicated pilot and list clearly which KMS integrations are supported (by 10/22)
- Vivek: draft a high-level sketch of Private deployment options and rough cost bands (by 10/27)

Please reply to confirm the timeline and we can set a short follow-up demo for the ops/procurement folks.

Best,
Sean

Subject: Re: Post-call recap — deployment gating items (SSO / KMS / logs)

Thanks, Sean — good summary. A few clarifications from our side:—

1) HSM requirement: For any environment that will process customer PII we require HSM-backed key material (FIPS 140-2 Level 3 or equivalent). Our security team can consider a cloud‑HSM if the instance is dedicated to us; multi‑tenant managed keys don’t meet the bar.

2) SSO: Okta SAML + SCIM is mandatory. We also want an SP-initiated SSO flow for the Redwood Console and token-based API auth mapped to our IdP groups.

3) Logging: 7 years retention minimum. Logs must be exportable to our Splunk instance (syslog or API export) with a tamper-evident retention option. We need per-request metadata (timestamp, model-id, route, requestor-id, response tokens).

4) Pilot ask: We are open to a 90-day Dedicated pilot to validate latency and throughput, provided we have a clear migration path to Private with minimal work and a rollback/fallback SLA. Procurement is roughly aligned to Q1 budget but we may execute a PO for the pilot sooner.

Procurement contact: ProcureOps (procure@medfoundry.com) — they will lead on PO terms and NDAs.

Can Laura share the exact KMS integration points and whether a dedicated cloud‑HSM (single-tenant) is supported under your Dedicated SKU? Also please provide an example retention clause you’d accept for logs.

Regards,
Erin
Erin Cole
Head of IT Security, MedFoundry

Hi Erin / team —

Thanks for the clear asks — a few technical clarifications from the solutions side:—

1) Dedicated pilot capabilities
- SSO: Full SAML + SCIM support with group mappings into Redwood RBAC. We can configure SP-initiated and IdP-initiated flows.
- KMS: Dedicated supports BYOK via common cloud KMS providers (AWS KMS, Google KMS, Azure Key Vault). For Dedicated, we do not currently provision a single-tenant (physically isolated) HSM per customer in the multi-tenant Dedicated cluster. However, we can integrate with a customer-managed cloud-HSM key (e.g., AWS CloudHSM) if you provide network connectivity and allowlist. There are additional networking controls we’ll need (VPC peering or private link).

2) Private options for HSM
- Private VPC or on‑prem appliances are the right path if you require FIPS-level HSMs physically dedicated to your keys. Private supports direct HSM integration and retention policies enforced by local log export and immutable storage options.

3) Logs & retention
- We can stream audit logs in near-real-time to your Splunk via secure syslog/HTTPS. For 7-year retention and tamper-evidence, Private gives you direct control; for Dedicated we support export and lifecycle policies but immutable WORM storage would need to be owned by MedFoundry (we can push to your S3 with object lock enabled).

4) Cost/ops note
- Rough delta: Dedicated pilot (90d) — nominal pilot hosting & engineering support credits. Moving to Private with HSM will have an uplift (est. 2–3x infra cost depending on HSM sizing). I attached a brief cost sketch.

Action items I’ll take:
- Provide a KMS integration checklist + network allowlist requirements (by 10/23)
- Provide sample log export configuration and example retention clause language (by 10/24)

If a pilot is acceptable, we’ll document the migration path and produce a minimal migration checklist so the move from Dedicated → Private remains predictable.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai

Attachments: deployment_cost_estimates.pdf (pdf)
